parties:
SHAHIDA BEGUM AND OTHERS.
v.
SAMSUL HAQUE DEAD HIS LEGAL HEIRS 1(A) KORFULER NESSA AND OTHERS
full_judgment: 10. Having gone through the judgment of the Courts below and other materials, it appears that specific contention of the petitioner was that summons was not served upon the petitioner No.1 and Ekramul Haque is not the brother's son of petitioner No.1 and as such purported service of summons upon Ekramul Haque on behalf of the petitioner No.1 is not service of summons in the eye of law. Further contention of the petitioner was that Abul Khair P.W.2 by giving evidence stated that he was not present at the purported service of summons. P.W.3 also stated that other 2 witnesses are not resident of village Vashanda and as such service of summons upon the petitioner is not valid service of summons. On the other hand O.P. W.2 who served the summons upon the petitioner No. 1 through his brother's son stated that he served summons upon the petitioner. The O. P.W.2 made declaration in his summons that summons was duly served upon the defendant which is presumption of due service and it has got evidentially value, although it is rebutable but such presumption is to be rebutted by cogent evidence. Another aspect of the case is that defendant No.1 who is the full brother of the petitioner has preferred appeal against the ex-parte judgment and decree, so, from that point also a presumption may be taken that since defendant No.1 and petitioner are full brother and sister there is no reason that the petitioner was not aware about the institution and disposal of the suit, appeal and other proceeding. So far onus regarding service of summons, initial onus rested upon the plaintiff so, that such summons was duly served upon the defendant, if the initial onus is discharged it is upon the defendant petitioner that summons was not duly served upon him but this particular case is rested on other vital aspects also. Admittedly the ex-parte decree has been challenged by filing appeal and the appellate Court also affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the revisional Court also affirmed discharged the rule by affirming the judgment and decree of the appellate Court and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal has been dismissed. On perusal of the case of Sajeda Khatun Vs. Mostafa Khatun reported in 28 DLR 221 it appears that when an ex-parte decree passed by the trial Court is it merged in the decree of the appellate court, the formar has no jurisdiction to amend the ex-parte decree. In the case of Md. Wasiq Khan Vs. Md. Sabiq Khan and another reported in in 31 DLR AD 51. similar view has been reiterated in paragraph No.18 which is hereunder: "On a review of the decisions and the discussion on the question set out, the following propositions seem to be well settled: Where a defendant against whom an ex-parte decree is passed applies under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure to set it aside and at the same time prefers an appeal from it, the Calcutta High Court has held that notwithstanding the pendency of appeal the original Court may proceed with the application.
